parts.text: The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A grotesque disfigured old man with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin with age spots, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red-rimmed lids, a large ear with a fat hanging lobe, thick neck, hunched broad shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Head type: a huge tall lumpy dome skull with dents and bumps, like the master reference, deep dark-brown clay skin, wild spiky grey hair tufts, a stitched scar across the scalp, a heavily stretched earlobe on his visible ear holding a large shiny polished silver steel tunnel gauge, a hollow metal ring about an inch wide with flared rims that you can see straight through, hanging just below the ear. No mask: his disfigured face is bare, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red lids, a crooked broken nose and rotten yellow teeth. Wearing a long battered dark plum greatcoat with a ragged high collar, honey stains down the front and a few clay bees crawling on the shoulder, he wields a LONG-HANDLED garden string trimmer (weed whacker) in BOTH hands, fitted with a gleaming GOLDEN saw blade instead of trimmer line. It is a long thin straight steel pole, longer than his arm: at the near end a yellow-and-black motor housing with a pistol trigger grip held in his right fist, a black D-shaped loop handle clamped halfway along the pole held in his left fist, and at the far end of the pole a small scuffed yellow guard over a toothed solid-gold saw disc flecked with blood. It is NOT a hand-held circular saw or angle grinder; no brand name, no lettering, a long woodcutter's axe slung on his back, head above his shoulder. A slate-grey pressed-clay backdrop. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, his body is in three-quarter view and his head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Both hands hold the weed whacker, one fist on the rear trigger grip and the other on the loop handle; the shaft angled up across his body so the golden saw blade is raised beside his head, the whole tool inside the frame; neither hand hangs empty. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, long finger blades, clawed glove with four long knives, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora
